learning_outcomes.text: Comprehension and mastery of basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application for solving engineering problems.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Demonstrate skills for planning, organization, and strategy.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Possess the ability to make decisions.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations.
Ability to generate new ideas (creativity).
Ability to work autonomously.
Show initiative and entrepreneurial spirit.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Motivation for achievement.

Assimilate and understand the concepts of Physics, specifically those related to Thermodynamics and Electromagnetism, as well as establish relationships between them and apply them practically in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Develop skills and techniques for solving simple physical problems.
Know and practice some basic techniques of the Physics laboratory and learn to correctly interpret the results obtained in the experiments.

syllabus_topics: Internal energy. First law of Thermodynamics
Thermodynamic processes of an ideal gas
Second law of Thermodynamics. Heat engines.
TOPIC 3. ELECTRIC FIELD IN A VACUUM
Electric potential energy and electric potential
TOPIC 4. ELECTRIC FIELD IN MATERIAL MEDIA
Force of a magnetic field on a current
Magnetic field in material media. Magnets
TOPIC 7. ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION AND ALTERNATING CURRENT
teaching_methods: Exposition of topics using multimedia projector and/or blackboard
Resolution of problems with statements and solutions provided in advance for prior student work
Execution of laboratory practicals in pairs
Individual or small group academic tutorials (in-person or online)
assessment_rules: Evaluation consists of several continuous assessment tests and assignments (40%), mandatory laboratory work (20%), and a global exam (40%). Continuous assessment tests and laboratory practicals are not recoverable in the second call. The laboratory work requires a minimum grade of 3 out of 10, and the global exam requires a minimum of 4 out of 10. The global exam can be retaken in the second call, and students who passed in the first call may repeat it to improve their grade by notifying the coordinator in advance. For exceptional evaluation, students must attend at least 40% of lab sessions and will be assessed via a 40% written exam (min 4/10), a 40% oral theoretical-practical test (min 3/10), and 20% laboratory work (min 3/10), with an overall weighted average of at least 5/10.
